- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) and forecast is low, model underestimates future price; increase forecast by 10–30% for high-sentiment periods.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.33) and forecast is high, model overestimates; reduce forecast by 15–40% for low-sentiment periods.
- After a sharp spike in forecast (e.g., >3x mean), model often overcorrects; apply a “cool-down” rule: reduce forecast by 20–50% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- Model tends to underpredict mean-reversion in 30-day horizon; if recent 7-day average is >1.5x 30-day average, adjust forecast downward by 10–25%.
- Forecast errors are more severe when sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00 → 0.67); apply smoothing filter to reduce volatility in forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds 3x historical 30-day mean, model is likely overconfident; reduce forecast by 20–40% unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- If sentiment history shows a recent “bullish reversal” (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00 → 0.67), model often misreads trend; adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift, not historical mean.
